title: NY State Senate · District 22
area: South Brooklyn, including Borough Park, Midwood, Gravesend, Bensonhurst and Mapleton.

context.text: Nachman Caller defeated Bernard Vaiselberg 535 votes (50.9%) to 517 votes (49.1%) in the June 23, 2026 Republican primary for this seat; the result was too close to call on election night and was contested by Vaiselberg before being certified by the Board of Elections. Caller also held the Conservative Party line without a primary contest.

Incumbent Sam Sutton first won the seat in a May 20, 2025 special election, defeating Nachman Caller and Bernard Vaiselberg (who ran that time as an independent write-in), after longtime Senator Simcha Felder did not seek re-election.

summary.text: Sam Sutton is the Democratic incumbent state senator for District 22, a South Brooklyn seat with a large Sephardic Jewish community. He won a May 2025 special election after Simcha Felder left the seat, and before that spent over 30 years as a lay leader of Sephardic communal and educational organizations. He faces Republican/Conservative nominee Nachman Caller in the general election.

background.text: Graduated Yeshiva of Flatbush (1967) and Yeshiva University (1971).
Led his family business for more than three decades before selling it to an international conglomerate.
Served over 30 years on the board of Sephardic Bikur Holim, a Brooklyn social-services organization, including five years as its president.
Co-founder and board chair of Teach NYS, an organization that advocates for government funding for nonpublic schools such as yeshivas and Jewish day schools.
Appointed by Governor George Pataki to the CUNY Board of Trustees, serving from 2006 to 2012.

priorities.text: Said he ran because "given our community's growth and needs, we deserve a representative who is deeply rooted in our community and understands its dynamics."
Has made funding and security for yeshivas and other nonpublic schools a central focus, including sponsoring buffer-zone legislation and securing state nonpublic-school-security grant funding.

positions.summary: Co-founded and chairs Teach NYS, which advocates for state funding to support nonpublic schools including yeshivas.

record.text: Sponsored S8599 (2025-26), which would create a 25-foot buffer zone restricting demonstrations near houses of worship and reproductive health care facilities; referred to the Senate Codes Committee on January 7, 2026 and has not received a floor vote.

Joined Governor Hochul and other officials at a November 2025 event condemning antisemitic vandalism at a Brooklyn yeshiva and cemetery, at which the state announced $20 million in additional funding for the nonpublic school safety equipment grant program.
Serves on the Senate Aging, Education, Health, Disabilities, NYC Education and Social Services committees.
Recorded as excused, and did not vote, on the full slate of Senate floor votes taken June 1, 2026, including the Grid Reliability and Energy Affordability Transition (GREAT) Act, which passed 39-21.

candidates.name: Nachman Caller
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 23, 2026 Republican primary against Bernard Vaiselberg, 50.9% to 49.1%; also holds the Conservative Party line.

summary.text: Nachman Caller is a Borough Park real estate attorney and Republican district leader running for the second time for this seat, after losing the May 2025 special election to Sam Sutton. He narrowly won the 2026 Republican primary over Bernard Vaiselberg and also carries the Conservative Party line.

background.text: Graduated with honors from Columbia Law School.
Describes himself as a real estate attorney and advocate for the Borough Park community with over three decades of service.
Ran for State Assembly in 2014 on the Republican and Housing & Jobs Party lines, losing to incumbent Dov Hikind.
Lost the May 2025 special election for this Senate seat to Sam Sutton.

priorities.text: Campaign site describes him as pledging to "champion rezoning for new housing development," reduce regulations that hinder housing growth, and secure fair city and state resources for the district.
priorities.quote: An Advocate we can count on—a fighter we can get behind.

priorities.text: Campaign platform pledges to "defend parents' rights to determine their children's education" and to "advocate tirelessly for the independence of our Yeshivas."

positions.summary: Campaign platform pledges to champion rezoning for new housing development and reduce regulations that hinder housing growth, citing his record developing thousands of housing units in Borough Park.
